```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import itertools as _it

DOC = "PCR-003"
UO = "bioreactor"
UO_TITLE = "Production Bioreactor (Step 3)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ----------------
RESP = D.responses(UO)                       # five measured culture attributes
SCRF = D.screening_factors(UO)               # screening factor set
RSMF = D.rsm_factors(UO)                     # response-surface factor subset
LAB = D.RESP_LABEL
CQA_KEYS = ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high_mannose",
            "aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "hcp", "residual_dna"]

n_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening")
n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
cp_scr = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening")
cp_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
n_fact_scr = n_scr - cp_scr
n_resp = len(RESP)
n_scrf = len(SCRF)
n_rsmf = len(RSMF)

# parameters and their outcome classification
prm = report_params(UO)
n_param = len(prm)
n_multi = int((prm["Study"] == "multivariate").sum())
n_uni = n_param - n_multi
cls_n = prm["Class"].value_counts().to_dict()
n_wccpp = cls_n.get("WC-CPP", 0)
n_kpp = cls_n.get("KPP", 0)
n_gpp = cls_n.get("GPP", 0)
n_cpp = cls_n.get("CPP", 0)


def pset(f, attr="setpoint"):
    """Set-point / NOR / characterization-range edge of one parameter, from config."""
    p = CFG.unit_op(UO).param(f)
    return {"setpoint": p.setpoint, "nor_lo": p.nor[0], "nor_hi": p.nor[1],
            "lo": p.prange[0], "hi": p.prange[1]}[attr]


# width of the characterization range as a multiple of the NOR width
_wid = [(pset(f, "hi") - pset(f, "lo")) / (pset(f, "nor_hi") - pset(f, "nor_lo"))
        for f in SCRF]
wid_lo, wid_hi = min(_wid), max(_wid)
_wid_rsm = [(pset(f, "hi") - pset(f, "lo")) / (pset(f, "nor_hi") - pset(f, "nor_lo"))
            for f in RSMF]
wid_rsm_lo, wid_rsm_hi = min(_wid_rsm), max(_wid_rsm)

# fitted models
fit_s = {r: D.fit(UO, "screening", r) for r in RESP}
fit_r = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RESP}
scr_terms = len(fit_s[RESP[0]]["names"]) + 1
scr_resid_df = int(fit_s[RESP[0]]["model"].df_resid)
scr_pred_hi = max(f["predR2"] for f in fit_s.values())
rsm_terms = len(fit_r[RESP[0]]["names"]) + 1
rsm_resid_df = int(fit_r[RESP[0]]["model"].df_resid)
rsm_pe_df = int(fit_r[RESP[0]]["df_pe"])
rsm_lof_df = int(fit_r[RESP[0]]["df_lof"])
rsm_r2_lo = min(f["R2"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_r2_hi = max(f["R2"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_adj_lo = min(f["adjR2"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_pred_lo = min(f["predR2"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_pred_hi = max(f["predR2"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_lof_p_lo = min(f["p_lof"] for f in fit_r.values())
rsm_adj_lo_r = LAB[min(fit_r, key=lambda r: fit_r[r]["adjR2"])]
rsm_pred_lo_r = LAB[min(fit_r, key=lambda r: fit_r[r]["predR2"])]
rsm_lof_lo_r = LAB[min(fit_r, key=lambda r: fit_r[r]["p_lof"])]

# effect / coefficient lookups (grounded accessors used by the inline expressions)
_sc = {r: D.screening_effects_df(UO, r).set_index("Term") for r in RESP}
_rc = {r: D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, r).set_index("Term") for r in RESP}


def sc(resp, term, col="Effect"):
    return float(_sc[resp].loc[term, col])


def rc(resp, term, col="Coef."):
    return float(_rc[resp].loc[term, col])


def n_sig(resp, kind="screening"):
    d = _sc[resp] if kind == "screening" else _rc[resp]
    return int((d["p-value"] < 0.05).sum())


def rn(key):
    """Prose name of a response, taken from the model's own label."""
    return LAB[key].split(" (")[0].lower()


def jn(keys):
    """Join response names into a prose list."""
    n = [rn(k) for k in keys]
    return n[0] if len(n) == 1 else ", ".join(n[:-1]) + " and " + n[-1]


# which screening models explain more than noise overall (model F test)
_scrfit = D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
scr_f_sig = jn([r for r in RESP if _scrfit.loc[LAB[r], "p-value"] < 0.05])
scr_f_ns = jn([r for r in RESP if _scrfit.loc[LAB[r], "p-value"] >= 0.05])

# centre-point reproducibility
cc_r = D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm")
cc_s = D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening")
cc_hi = cc_r.loc[cc_r["%CV"].idxmax()]
cc_lo = cc_r.loc[cc_r["%CV"].idxmin()]
cc_hi2 = cc_r.sort_values("%CV").iloc[-2]
cc_s_hi = cc_s.loc[cc_s["%CV"].idxmax()]
cc_s_lo = cc_s.loc[cc_s["%CV"].idxmin()]
cc_s_lo_at_rsm = float(cc_r.loc[cc_r["Response"] == cc_s_lo["Response"], "%CV"].iloc[0])

# commercial-scale capability
capb = cap[cap.key.isin(CQA_KEYS)].copy()
tight = capb.loc[capb["Cpk"].idxmin()]
wide = capb.loc[capb["Cpk"].idxmax()]
_cpl = float(tight["Cpl"]) if pd.notna(tight["Cpl"]) else float("inf")
_cpu = float(tight["Cpu"]) if pd.notna(tight["Cpu"]) else float("inf")
tight_side = "lower" if _cpl <= _cpu else "upper"
tight_margin = float(tight["mean"] - tight["acc_low"]) if tight_side == "lower" \
    else float(tight["acc_high"] - tight["mean"])
tight_other = float(tight["acc_high"] - tight["mean"]) if tight_side == "lower" \
    else float(tight["mean"] - tight["acc_low"])
cpk_min = float(capb["Cpk"].min())

# design-space evaluation over the four response-surface factors
_lv = 21
_g = np.linspace(-1, 1, _lv)
_mesh = np.array(list(_it.product(_g, repeat=n_rsmf)))
_coded = {f: _mesh[:, i] for i, f in enumerate(RSMF)}
ds_pred = {r: D.predict(UO, r, coded=_coded) for r in RESP}
ds_in = {r: D.meets_acceptance(UO, r, ds_pred[r]) for r in RESP}
ds_ok = np.ones(len(_mesh), dtype=bool)
for r in RESP:
    ds_ok &= ds_in[r]
ds_pts = len(_mesh)
ds_excl = int((~ds_ok).sum())
_bindk = [r for r in RESP if not ds_in[r].all()]
ds_bind = LAB[_bindk[0]] if _bindk else ""
_worst = int(np.argmax(ds_pred[_bindk[0]])) if _bindk else 0
wc = {f: float(D.to_natural(UO, f, _mesh[_worst, i])) for i, f in enumerate(RSMF)}
wc_val = float(ds_pred[_bindk[0]][_worst]) if _bindk else float("nan")
bind_lo, bind_hi, _bt = D.acceptance_for(UO, _bindk[0])
wc_over = wc_val - bind_hi

# the same models evaluated at the corners of the normal operating ranges
_nor = np.array(list(_it.product(*[(pset(f, "nor_lo"), pset(f, "nor_hi")) for f in RSMF])))
_nor_nat = {f: _nor[:, i] for i, f in enumerate(RSMF)}
nor_pred = {r: D.predict(UO, r, natural=_nor_nat) for r in RESP}
nor_tbl = pd.DataFrame(
    [[LAB[r], f"{D.acceptance_for(UO, r)[0]:g}–{D.acceptance_for(UO, r)[1]:g}",
      D.acceptance_for(UO, r)[2].replace("_", " "),
      float(nor_pred[r].min()), float(nor_pred[r].max())] for r in RESP],
    columns=["Response", "Acceptance", "Criterion", "Min over NOR corners",
             "Max over NOR corners"])
nor_bind_max = float(nor_pred[_bindk[0]].max()) if _bindk else float("nan")
nor_bind_margin = bind_hi - nor_bind_max
nor_corners = len(_nor)

# fitted response at the set-point
_sp = {f: [pset(f)] for f in RSMF}
sp_pred = {r: float(D.predict(UO, r, natural=_sp)[0]) for r in RESP}

# nominal process performance of the step
_ps = csv("process_summary.csv")
bio = _ps[_ps.step == 3].iloc[0]

# deviation impact, evaluated on the fitted model (DEV-003-01 probe offset)
dev1_coded = float(D.to_coded(UO, "co2", pset("co2") + dev_003_01_offset_mmhg))
_sp_off = dict(_sp)
_sp_off["co2"] = [pset("co2") + dev_003_01_offset_mmhg]
dev1_shift = {r: float(D.predict(UO, r, natural=_sp_off)[0]) - sp_pred[r] for r in RESP}
dev1_worst_r = max(dev1_shift, key=lambda r: abs(dev1_shift[r]))
dev1_worst = abs(dev1_shift[dev1_worst_r])
dev1_sd = float(cc_r.loc[cc_r["Response"] == LAB[dev1_worst_r], "SD"].iloc[0])

# aggregate: culture level at the centre point against the drug-substance mean
agg_cp = float(cc_r.loc[cc_r["Response"] == LAB["aggregates_hmw"], "Mean"].iloc[0])
agg_ds = float(capb.loc[capb.key == "aggregates_hmw", "mean"].iloc[0])
agg_ratio = agg_cp / agg_ds

# DEV-003-02: delivered feed volume after the pump offset
feed_sp = pset("feed_vol")
dev2_delivered = feed_sp * (1 - dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct / 100.0)

# analytical method register for Appendix D
AMV_ANALYTE = {"AMV-3010": ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high_mannose"],
               "AMV-3011": ["aggregates_hmw"],
               "AMV-3012": ["hcp"],
               "AMV-3013": ["acidic_variants"],
               "AMV-3014": ["residual_dna"]}
_mth = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")
_amv_name = dict(AMV_REFS)
_rows = []
for _aid, _keys in AMV_ANALYTE.items():
    _an = ", ".join(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == k].iloc[0]["cqa"] for k in _keys)
    _un = cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == _keys[0]].iloc[0]["unit"]
    if _aid in _mth.index:
        _m = _mth.loc[_aid]
        _pr, _lq = f"{_m.precision_pct:g}", f"{_m.loq:g} {_m.loq_unit}"
    else:
        _pr = _lq = "per validation report"
    _rows.append([_aid, _amv_name[_aid], _an, _un, _pr, _lq])
amv_tbl = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Reference", "Method", "Attribute reported",
                                       "Reportable unit", "Precision (%RSD)", "LOQ"])

# compact classification table
cls_tbl = prm[["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Char. range", "Study", "Class"]]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

The production bioreactor is characterized, and the multivariate region defined in this
report supports the operating ranges proposed for commercial manufacture. A-Mab is
produced by fed-batch culture of a humanized IgG1 cell line at a working volume of
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L. The step establishes the glycan, charge
variant and aggregate attributes of the drug substance, so it carries most of the
product-quality risk in the upstream process. The studies were executed on a qualified
scale-down model under the paired protocol PCP-003, following the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011], the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq11], and the quality-attribute and risk framework of the A-Mab case study
[@amab2009].

The study carried `{python} n_param` parameters, on the risk basis established in RA-001.
Of those, `{python} n_multi` were studied multivariately, in a screening design of
`{python} n_scr` runs followed by a response-surface design of `{python} n_rsm` runs, and
the remaining `{python} n_uni` were assessed one at a time. The screening design identified
the active factors. The response-surface model is the predictive model and the basis of the
design space, and it accounts for between `{python} pct(rsm_r2_lo)` and
`{python} pct(rsm_r2_hi)` of the observed variation in the `{python} n_resp` measured
attributes, with lack of fit not significant for any of them.

One corner of the characterized region is excluded from the design space. With culture pH,
culture duration and pCO₂ all at their low edges and culture temperature at its high edge,
the fitted model predicts `{python} ds_bind.lower()` of `{python} f"{wc_val:.2f}"` %,
which is `{python} f"{wc_over:.2f}"` percentage points above the upper acceptance limit of
`{python} f"{bind_hi:g}"` %. That exclusion covers `{python} ds_excl` of the
`{python} f"{ds_pts:,}"` grid points examined across the four response-surface factors.
Across the `{python} nor_corners` corners of the normal operating ranges the highest
predicted value of the same attribute is `{python} f"{nor_bind_max:.1f}"` %, which leaves
`{python} f"{nor_bind_margin:.1f}"` percentage points to the limit. The design space is the
characterized region with that one corner removed, and the normal operating ranges sit well
inside it.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated from `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"`
simulated batches with every parameter varying inside its normal operating range. All seven
attributes the step sets meet their acceptance criteria. `{python} tight["cqa"]` carries the
tightest capability, with a one-sided Cpk of `{python} f"{tight['Cpk']:.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{tight_margin:.2f}"` percentage points between the predicted mean and the
binding `{python} tight_side` limit. Two deviations were recorded during execution
(§13). Both were investigated, impact assessed and retained, and neither changed a
parameter classification or the boundaries of the operating region.

The step does not control host cell protein, residual DNA or aggregate at the drug
substance on its own. Those attributes are generated in the culture and are then reduced by
the purification train, and the clearance credited to the downstream steps is reported in
PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. The capability figures given here rest on a qualified
scale-down model with all parameters held inside their normal operating ranges. They are
not a commercial-scale confirmation, which is the object of the process performance
qualification. This report rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced in a recombinant mammalian cell
line. Its primary mechanism of action is antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity, so the
N-linked glycan profile of the molecule is directly linked to efficacy and is treated as a
set of critical quality attributes throughout development [@amab2009]. The drug substance
process is a platform process, and its unit operations and their principal roles are given
in @tbl-steps.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug substance process train, with the principal role of each unit "
      "operation in the control strategy. {#tbl-steps}")
```

The production bioreactor is the only step of the drug substance process at which product
quality attributes are formed. The glycosylation and charge variant distributions are
established inside the cell and in the culture fluid, and the platform purification train
does not modify them. Protein A capture, cation exchange and anion exchange chromatography
separate on affinity and on charge, and none of them discriminates between the glycoforms
of an intact antibody. What the downstream steps do is remove process impurities and reduce
the aggregate that leaves the bioreactor, and that clearance is characterized in the
reports for those steps.

The step is operated as a fed-batch culture at a working volume of
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L, with pH, temperature and dissolved oxygen
under closed-loop control, pCO₂ monitored continuously, and nutrient feed delivered on a
fixed schedule. At the
nominal set-point the culture reaches a peak viable cell density of
`{python} f"{bio.peak_vcd_e6:.1f}"` × 10⁶ cells/mL and is harvested at a viability of
`{python} f"{bio.final_viability_pct:.0f}"` % after
`{python} f"{pset('duration'):g}"` days, giving a titre of
`{python} f"{bio.titer_g_per_l:.2f}"` g/L and
`{python} f"{bio.product_mass_g/1000:.0f}"` kg of antibody in the harvested culture fluid.
The five attributes measured across the characterization studies are afucosylation,
galactosylation, high mannose, acidic charge variants and high molecular weight aggregate.
Host cell protein and residual DNA are also generated here, and both are governed at the
drug substance by downstream clearance as much as by culture conditions.

## Objectives

This report presents the executed characterization of the production bioreactor against the
objectives set in PCP-003. Those objectives were:

(i) to quantify the relationship between each studied process parameter and the quality
    attributes the step forms, across ranges wider than the intended operating ranges;
(ii) to define a multivariate operating region over the well-controlled culture parameters
     in which every attribute in scope remains within its acceptance criterion;
(iii) to establish proven acceptable ranges for each parameter against each attribute it
      governs, both at the set-point and under normal operating variation of the other
      parameters;
(iv) to classify every parameter carried into the study according to the decision logic of
     SOP-4001, on the basis of the demonstrated effects and the risk of leaving the
     operating region; and
(v) to justify the ranges and controls carried forward into Stage 2 and into the overall
    control strategy consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the sense of the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced development approach described in
ICH Q8 and ICH Q11, in which prior knowledge and a formal risk assessment direct the
experimental work, and the outcome is an operating region and a control strategy rather
than a set of fixed points [@ichq8; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as
described in ICH Q9 and applied throughout the A-Mab case study, so an attribute is
assigned a level from very low to very high and the attributes at high and very high
criticality are called critical [@ichq9; @amab2009].

No viral clearance claim is made for this step. The viral safety evaluation is modular and
rests on the low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration steps, and it is
assessed under ICH Q5A in PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009 [@ichq5a]. Nothing in this report
contributes to that claim.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The fed-batch platform used for A-Mab has an extensive performance history. It has
supported three previous humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) through
clinical supply and commercial manufacture, and the medium, feed strategy and control
scheme carried into A-Mab are the platform ones [@amab2009]. The consequence for this study
is that the characterization confirms and bounds mechanisms that are already understood,
instead of discovering them. The acceptance limits for aggregate and for host cell protein
are themselves set from prior clinical experience with X-Mab.

The platform establishes what each culture parameter is expected to do. Culture pH sets the
intracellular and Golgi pH, which governs the activity of the glycosyltransferases and the
fucosyltransferase, so pH is expected to move afucosylation, galactosylation and high
mannose together. Culture temperature changes cell-specific productivity and the residence
time of the molecule in the secretory pathway, so a lower temperature is expected to raise
terminal galactosylation. Dissolved carbon dioxide acidifies the intracellular compartment
and is expected to suppress galactosylation and, through the same route, the deamidation
that produces acidic charge variants. Osmolality acts on cell-specific productivity and on
the same enzymes, but more weakly. Culture duration acts through the decline in viability
that occurs late in a fed-batch culture, which releases intracellular enzymes and host cell
protein into the culture fluid and raises aggregate.

Two of these expectations are not independent. pH and duration act on the same
glycosylation machinery at different points in the culture, so an interaction between them
was anticipated and was the main reason for taking the study beyond one factor at a time.
The study was designed to confirm or refute each of these expectations (§5.2), and §5.4
returns to them against the fitted models.

## Quality attributes in scope

The attributes this step sets are listed in @tbl-cqa with their acceptance criteria and
their assigned criticality. The Tool #1 score is the product of impact and uncertainty, and
the attributes scored high or very high are treated as critical [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Quality attributes set by the production bioreactor, with acceptance criteria "
      "and assigned criticality. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

High mannose carries the highest score in the table, because its impact on clearance and
its residual uncertainty are both high, and it is the only attribute of the seven at very
high criticality. Afucosylation and galactosylation follow, both linked to potency through
antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement dependent cytotoxicity. Aggregate
is critical on immunogenicity grounds. Acidic charge variants and residual DNA score low,
which reflects a well characterized structure-function relationship in the first case and a
very large clearance margin in the second. Host cell protein sits between the two groups.

Three of the seven attributes are governed by more than one step. Aggregate leaving the
bioreactor is raised slightly during the low-pH hold and is then polished by cation
exchange, so the drug substance level reported in §8 is not attributable to culture
conditions alone (PCR-006, PCR-007). Host cell protein and residual DNA are generated in
the culture at levels several orders of magnitude above the drug substance criterion and
are cleared by Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-005, PCR-007, PCR-008).
This report characterizes the contribution the bioreactor makes to each of them, which is
the input level, and it makes no clearance claim.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 assessed every parameter of this step before any characterization run was executed,
using the risk ranking and filtering method of the A-Mab case study. Each parameter was
scored on its potential impact on a quality attribute and on its potential to interact with
other parameters, and the score determined the type of study assigned to it [@amab2009;
@ichq9]. Parameters with a credible route to a quality attribute and a credible interaction
went into the multivariate design. Parameters whose expected effect is on process
performance and not on product quality were assigned to univariate study. No parameter
of this step was left unstudied.

The assignment is reproduced in the classification table in §9, and the outcome was
`{python} n_multi` multivariate parameters (culture pH, culture temperature, pCO₂,
osmolality and culture duration) and `{python} n_uni` univariate ones (dissolved oxygen,
initial viable cell concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume).
The five multivariate parameters are the ones the risk assessment linked to the glycan,
charge variant and aggregate attributes, and they are also the parameters for which prior
knowledge predicts interactions.

The ranges studied are wider than the ranges the process will be run in. Each multivariate
characterization range is between `{python} f"{wid_lo:.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{wid_hi:.1f}"` times the width of the corresponding normal operating range,
which follows the practice of carrying the study well beyond the control range so that the
edges of the region are probed and not assumed [@amab2009]. Two constraints
bounded the expansion. The low pH edge was set where the platform cell line begins to lose
viability late in culture, and the high duration edge was set by the harvest criteria in
SOP-2003, since a culture cannot be held past the point at which viability falls below the
harvest limit. The resulting ranges are the knowledge space for this step, and they are
listed in @tbl-params.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

All characterization runs were executed on a qualified scale-down model of the commercial
bioreactor, and the warrant for applying the results to commercial scale rests on that
qualification. The scale-down system is a stirred-tank bioreactor of the same geometry and
with the same control capability as the commercial vessel, covering pH, dissolved oxygen,
temperature, agitation and nutrient addition. The scale-independent parameters (pH,
temperature, dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration and culture duration) were
operated at the values proposed for commercial operation. The scale-dependent parameters
(agitation rate, gas flow rates, headspace pressure and working volume) were set so that
the scale-down system matched commercial-scale performance and not commercial-scale
settings, which is the standard approach for a stirred-tank culture and is the approach
described in the case study [@amab2009].

Qualification followed SOP-1001. Replicate set-point runs on the scale-down system were
compared against commercial-scale engineering batches on the process performance
measures (peak viable cell density, harvest viability, titre) and on the full quality
panel, and the comparison and its acceptance criteria are reported in PCP-003. The model is
qualified for the ranges characterized here and for the cell line and medium used here. It
is not qualified for a change of medium platform, and any such change would require the
comparison to be repeated.

The centre-point replicates executed within each design serve a second purpose. They give
an estimate of pure error that is independent of the fitted model, which is what makes the
lack-of-fit test in §5.3 a real test and not a restatement of the residual variance.
Their reproducibility is reported in §5.1.

## Cell line, media and culture operation

The production culture was operated per SOP-2003. Cells were expanded through the seed
train, inoculated into the production vessel at the target initial viable cell
concentration, and cultured in fed-batch mode with nutrient feed-1 delivered on the
platform schedule. Basal medium and feed were prepared per SOP-2004 from released lots.
Culture pH was controlled by carbon dioxide sparge and base addition, temperature by the
vessel jacket, and dissolved oxygen by a gas cascade (SOP-2003). Harvest was triggered by the culture
duration under study, subject to the viability floor in SOP-2003.

Inputs that are controlled to a platform specification were not characterized here. The
working cell bank, the basal medium formulation, the feed formulation and the gas supplies
are identity tested and released against their specifications, and their control is a
control on materials and not a process parameter. The nominal fed-batch profile at the
set-point is shown in @fig-timecourse, and it is the reference against which each designed
run was assessed for normal culture behaviour.

![Nominal production-bioreactor profile at the set-point: viable cell density, culture viability and product titre over the fed-batch culture.](../outputs/figures/fig_bioreactor_timecourse.png){#fig-timecourse}

## Analytical methods

Every attribute reported here was measured by a validated method. @tbl-methods lists the
procedures and method validation reports that apply to this step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=SOP_REFS, amvs=AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Controlled procedures and validated analytical methods applied to the production "
      "bioreactor characterization. {#tbl-methods}")
```

The three glycan attributes were measured on a single released N-glycan map by 2-AB
labelled HILIC-UPLC (SOP-3010, AMV-3010), which reports afucosylation, galactosylation and
high mannose from one injection. Size variants were measured by SEC-HPLC (SOP-3011,
AMV-3011) and are reported as percent high molecular weight. Charge variants were measured
by icIEF (SOP-3013, AMV-3013) and are reported as the summed acidic peak area. Host cell
protein was measured by a platform ELISA (SOP-3012, AMV-3012) and residual DNA by qPCR
(SOP-3014, AMV-3014). Method performance is summarized in Appendix D, and the full
validation data are in the AMV reports.

Assay precision matters to the interpretation of the smaller effects. The glycan map has a
precision of `{python} f"{amv_3010_precision:g}"` % RSD and the host cell protein ELISA a
precision of `{python} f"{amv_3012_precision:g}"` % RSD, so the assay resolves a fraction
of a percentage point on any of the three glycan attributes at the levels they are reported
at. Reproducibility between runs is the wider quantity, since it carries the biological
variation of the culture as well as the analytical variation. A shift of about one
percentage point in a glycan attribute therefore becomes interpretable through replication
or through a fitted model, and not from a single determination. §5.1 separates the
analytical contribution from the process contribution using the centre-point replicates.

## Sampling plan

Each designed run was sampled daily for viable cell density, viability, metabolites and
titre, which supports the assessment of normal culture behaviour but is not part of the
designed analysis. The characterization responses were measured on the harvested culture
fluid of each run, taken at the culture duration assigned to that run and clarified before
analysis. One harvest sample per run was tested against the full panel, so each run
contributes one observation per response.

Centre-point runs were replicated within each design. The screening design carried
`{python} cp_scr` centre points and the response-surface design carried
`{python} cp_rsm`, all executed at the set-point of every factor. Replicating at the centre
instead of at a corner keeps the pure-error estimate at the condition the process will
actually run at, and it is the condition for which prior process history gives an
independent expectation.

## Statistical methods

All factors were analysed on a coded scale, in which the set-point of a factor is zero and
the edges of its characterization range are minus one and plus one. Coding puts the
estimates on a common footing, so that an effect is the change in the response across the
full characterization range of that factor and effects can be compared between parameters
with different units [@amab2009].

The two designs answer different questions and are analysed differently. The screening
design was analysed by ordinary least squares with all main effects and all two-factor
interactions, and an effect is reported as twice the fitted coefficient on the coded
factor. Its purpose is to identify which factors are active. The response-surface design
was analysed with a full quadratic model in the factors carried forward, which adds the
squared terms needed to describe curvature, and it is the model used for prediction, for
the design space and for the proven acceptable ranges. A significance level of α = 0.05 was
used throughout.

Model adequacy was assessed on four measures (SOP-1002). R² and adjusted R² describe how much of the
observed variation the model accounts for, with the adjustment penalising terms that do not
earn their degrees of freedom. Predicted R², computed from the PRESS statistic by leaving
each run out in turn, describes how the model performs on data it has not seen. The overall
F test asks whether the model as a whole explains more than noise. Finally, the residual
variance was partitioned into lack of fit and pure error using the centre-point replicates,
and a significant lack of fit would mean the model form is wrong even where its coefficients
are well estimated. A factor with no significant term for a given response is treated as
having no demonstrated effect on that response over the range studied.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, with every parameter drawn independently
within its normal operating range and the fitted models used to predict each attribute. The
capability index is one sided and is reported against the binding acceptance limit for each
attribute.

Proven acceptable ranges were computed for each attribute against each response-surface
factor, under two analyses. The first holds the other factors at their set-points and
evaluates the fitted model across the parameter's characterization range. The second varies
the other factors within their normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo of the same model,
and requires the 95 % predictive interval of the attribute to stay within acceptance, so it
is the more demanding of the two. Both are reported in §7.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The design covers `{python} n_param` parameters, and @tbl-params gives the set-point,
normal operating range, characterization range, study type and final classification of
each. The classification column is an outcome of this study and is argued parameter by
parameter in §9. The characterization range is the range over which the parameter was
actually varied, and it is the edge of the knowledge space, not a proven acceptable range.
The proven acceptable ranges are computed quantities and are given in §7.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
print()
print(": Production-bioreactor parameters, ranges, study type and final classification. "
      "{#tbl-params}")
```

The five multivariate factors are coded A to E for the analysis, and @tbl-legend gives the
mapping together with the design each factor appears in.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Coded factor legend for the production-bioreactor designs. {#tbl-legend}")
```

Each range was set from prior knowledge and not by a fixed multiple. The pH range of
`{python} f"{pset('pH','lo'):g}"` to `{python} f"{pset('pH','hi'):g}"` spans the region in
which the platform cell line grows and produces normally, and it is the widest range the
harvest viability criterion allows. The temperature range of
`{python} f"{pset('temperature','lo'):g}"` to `{python} f"{pset('temperature','hi'):g}"` °C
is set by the control capability of the commercial vessel, which holds the culture well
inside that band and makes a wider excursion implausible. The pCO₂ range of
`{python} f"{pset('co2','lo'):g}"` to `{python} f"{pset('co2','hi'):g}"` mmHg covers the
accumulation observed at commercial scale, where sparge efficiency falls with vessel size
and the upper part of the range is the realistic one. The osmolality range of
`{python} f"{pset('osmolality','lo'):g}"` to `{python} f"{pset('osmolality','hi'):g}"` mOsm
covers the drift produced by feeding and base addition over a full culture. The duration
range of `{python} f"{pset('duration','lo'):g}"` to
`{python} f"{pset('duration','hi'):g}"` days brackets the harvest window either side of the
set-point.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level design in the `{python} n_scrf` multivariate factors,
executed as a half fraction of resolution V with `{python} cp_scr` centre points, for
`{python} n_scr` runs in total. The generator sets culture duration as the product of the
other four factors, so the defining relation involves all five. At that resolution the main
effects are aliased only with four-factor interactions and the two-factor interactions only
with three-factor interactions, and effects of that order are not credible for a culture
process. The design therefore estimates all `{python} n_scrf` main effects and all ten
two-factor interactions clear of one another. The runs were randomised in execution order (SOP-1002).
The full design matrix with responses is given in Appendix A.

The `{python} n_fact_scr` factorial runs support a model of `{python} scr_terms` terms, so
the residual degrees of freedom come from the centre points alone. This is a deliberate
property of a screening design and it is the reason the screening fit is not used for
prediction. §5.2 reports what it does establish.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study was a face-centred central composite design in the
`{python} n_rsmf` factors carried forward from screening (culture pH, culture temperature,
culture duration and pCO₂), with `{python} cp_rsm` centre points, for `{python} n_rsm` runs
in total. The face-centred form places the axial runs on the faces of the cube and not
outside it, so no run is executed beyond the characterization range of any factor. That
choice keeps every prediction inside the region actually run, at the cost of a less precise
estimate of the pure quadratic terms.

Osmolality was not carried into the response-surface design. Its screening main effect is
the smallest of the five on galactosylation and on high mannose, which are the two
responses that drive the design space and the capability claim, and osmolality is held
close to its set-point in routine operation by the feed and base strategy. It was operated
at its set-point in every response-surface run, so the response-surface model, the design
space in §6 and the proven acceptable ranges in §7 all apply at osmolality within its
normal operating range. The parameter does appear in three significant galactosylation
interactions in the screening study, the largest of which is the interaction with culture
temperature at `{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','BD'):+.2f}"` percentage points. That term
is bounded by the screening estimate and by holding osmolality within its normal operating
range, and §9 classifies the parameter on that basis. The full response-surface matrix with
responses is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Four parameters were assessed one at a time: dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell
concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume. RA-001 ranked each of
them against process performance and not against a quality attribute, which is what
assigned them to single-factor study instead of the designed experiment. Each was operated
across its characterization range with all other parameters at their set-points, and the
harvest material was released against the same analytical panel.

The univariate work supports the operating ranges of those four parameters for process
performance. The results of the individual runs are held in the study record referenced by
PCP-003 and are not reproduced here, since no effect on a quality attribute was
demonstrated for any of the four over the range studied. The univariate work does not
extend the quality design space, which rests entirely on the multivariate studies, and it
is not used in §6 or §7.
The classifications that follow from it are given in §9.

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

Reproducibility at the centre point is good for three of the five responses and moderate
for galactosylation and high mannose. @tbl-cp gives the mean, standard deviation and
coefficient of variation of the
`{python} cp_rsm` response-surface centre points, which are the pure-error basis for the
lack-of-fit tests in §5.3.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm"))
print()
print(": Centre-point reproducibility of the response-surface design "
      "(n = " + str(cp_rsm) + " replicates at the set-point of every factor). {#tbl-cp}")
```

`{python} cc_hi["Response"]` is the least reproducible response, at
`{python} f"{cc_hi['%CV']:.1f}"` % CV, and `{python} cc_lo["Response"].lower()` the most
reproducible, at `{python} f"{cc_lo['%CV']:.1f}"` %. `{python} cc_hi2["Response"]` follows
close behind at `{python} f"{cc_hi2['%CV']:.1f}"` %, and that spread is the pure error the
galactosylation lack-of-fit test uses. Galactosylation is the response that defines the
design space, so its variation at the centre point is the term that test finally rests on.
The glycan map contributes
`{python} f"{amv_3010_precision:g}"` % RSD of that variation (§3.3), so most of the spread
in high mannose is biological in origin and not analytical. This matters for the interpretation
of the smaller effects, and it is the reason a shift of about one percentage point in a
glycan attribute is reported here as an effect only when the fitted model resolves it.

In the screening centre points, executed earlier in the campaign, the least reproducible
response is again `{python} cc_s_hi["Response"].lower()`, at
`{python} f"{cc_s_hi['%CV']:.1f}"` % CV. The ordering of the other four differs.
`{python} cc_s_lo["Response"]` is the most reproducible response in that set, at
`{python} f"{cc_s_lo['%CV']:.1f}"` %, against `{python} f"{cc_s_lo_at_rsm:.1f}"` % at the
response-surface centre points. Each figure rests on a handful of replicates, so the
difference belongs to the two replicate sets and not to the assay, and the lack-of-fit
tests that support the design space use the response-surface set.

## Screening: factor effects

The screening design separates the active factors from the inactive ones, and it does so
with different force from one response to another. @tbl-scrfit summarizes the fitted
screening models.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening"))
print()
print(": Screening model summary. The high R² values reflect a near-saturated design; "
      "predicted R² is negative for every response, which is why these models are not "
      "used for prediction. {#tbl-scrfit}")
```

The screening models fit the executed runs closely, and they have almost no predictive
latitude. Each model estimates `{python} scr_terms` terms from `{python} n_scr` runs, which
leaves `{python} scr_resid_df` residual degrees of freedom, and predicted R² is negative for
all `{python} n_resp` responses (the highest value is
`{python} f"{scr_pred_hi:.2f}"`). A negative predicted R² means the model predicts a
held-out run worse than the response mean would. The overall F test divides the panel as
well. It is significant for `{python} scr_f_sig`, and it does not reach significance for
`{python} scr_f_ns`, so the individual terms of those models are read as indicative and are
confirmed against the response-surface design in §5.3. The screening design identifies which
factors matter. The response-surface model is the predictive model and the basis of the
design space, and the effect magnitudes reported below are refined by it in §5.3.

@tbl-screff lists every screening term significant at α = 0.05, by response.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sig_rows = []
for _r in RESP:
    _d = D.screening_effects_df(UO, _r)
    _d = _d[_d["p-value"] < 0.05]
    for _t, _row in _d.iterrows():
        _sig_rows.append([LAB[_r], _row["Term"], _row["Effect"], _row["p-value"]])
show(pd.DataFrame(_sig_rows, columns=["Response", "Term", "Effect", "p-value"]))
print()
print(": Screening terms significant at α = 0.05, by response. An effect is the change in "
      "the response across the full characterization range of the factor. Factor codes "
      "are given in @tbl-legend. {#tbl-screff}")
```

Galactosylation is the most responsive attribute in the panel and the most heavily
interacting. Culture duration carries the largest single effect,
`{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','E'):+.1f}"` percentage points across its
characterization range, and the pH by duration interaction is almost as large at
`{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','AE'):+.1f}"`. pCO₂ and culture pH follow, at
`{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','C'):+.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','A'):+.1f}"`. Of the `{python} scr_terms - 1` estimable
terms, `{python} n_sig('galactosylation')` are significant, which is the clearest evidence in
the study that a one-factor-at-a-time treatment of this attribute would be misleading.

Acidic charge variants are governed mainly by pCO₂, whose effect of
`{python} f"{sc('acidic_variants','C'):+.1f}"` percentage points is the largest single
effect anywhere in the screening study. Culture pH and culture temperature follow at
`{python} f"{sc('acidic_variants','A'):+.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{sc('acidic_variants','B'):+.1f}"`, and osmolality contributes
`{python} f"{sc('acidic_variants','D'):+.1f}"`. The pCO₂ direction is the one §2.1
predicted, and the effect is negative as expected. §2.1 sets no direction for pH,
temperature or osmolality on this attribute, and the fitted pH direction is not the one
deamidation chemistry gives on its own (§5.4). The attribute is of very low criticality and
its acceptance range is wide, so these are large effects on a response that has room to
absorb them.

Afucosylation behaves differently, and the difference is informative. Only three of its
terms are significant, and the largest of them is the pH by duration interaction at
`{python} f"{sc('afucosylation','AE'):+.1f}"` percentage points, followed by culture
duration at `{python} f"{sc('afucosylation','E'):+.1f}"`. The main effect of pH is not
significant at α = 0.05 (p = `{python} f"{sc('afucosylation','A','p-value'):.3f}"`), yet pH
appears in two of the three significant terms. The effect of pH on afucosylation depends on
how long the culture is held, so the main effect on its own understates it. Aggregate is
the most straightforward of the five mechanistically, with culture pH at
`{python} f"{sc('aggregates_hmw','A'):+.2f}"` percentage points and culture duration at
`{python} f"{sc('aggregates_hmw','E'):+.2f}"` against an acceptance limit of
`{python} f"{D.acceptance_for(UO,'aggregates_hmw')[1]:g}"` %. The duration effect is
positive, which is the direction §2.1 expected from the decline in viability late in
culture.

High mannose is the sparsest response, and the null results are as useful as the
significant ones. Only culture pH and culture temperature have a significant effect, at
`{python} f"{sc('high_mannose','A'):+.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{sc('high_mannose','B'):+.1f}"` percentage points. pCO₂, osmolality and culture
duration show no significant effect on high mannose over the ranges screened, and no
interaction involving them is significant either. The screening model for this response
does not reach significance overall, so those null results are carried into the
response-surface design for confirmation before they are relied on. pCO₂ and culture
duration are retained in the knowledge space and are classified in §9 on the evidence from
both designs. Osmolality was not carried into the response-surface design, so its null
result on this attribute rests on the screening study alone (§4.3). High mannose is the
only attribute of very high criticality at this step, which is why §5.3 examines its
response surface in full.

Dissolved oxygen was held at its set-point throughout the designed runs and was not varied.
Platform manufacturing experience has established that dissolved oxygen does not influence
the glycan profile at any scale, so the factor was not carried into the multivariate work
and no further study of it is required.

Taken together, the `{python} n_scr` screening runs establish the multivariate design space
for the well-controlled culture parameters, and they confirm that the estimated effects hold
across the operating combinations the design did not itself execute.

## Response-surface models

A full quadratic model was fitted to each of the `{python} n_resp` responses over the four
factors carried into the response-surface design. @tbl-rsmfit summarizes model adequacy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "rsm"))
print()
print(": Response-surface model summary. Each model carries "
      + str(rsm_terms) + " terms fitted to " + str(n_rsm) + " runs. {#tbl-rsmfit}")
```

The models are adequate for all five responses and each of them retains predictive value on
runs it has not seen. R² ranges from `{python} f"{rsm_r2_lo:.2f}"` to
`{python} f"{rsm_r2_hi:.2f}"`, adjusted R² does not fall below
`{python} f"{rsm_adj_lo:.2f}"` (`{python} rsm_adj_lo_r.lower()`), and predicted R² does not
fall below `{python} f"{rsm_pred_lo:.2f}"` (`{python} rsm_pred_lo_r.lower()`), against a
highest value of `{python} f"{rsm_pred_hi:.2f}"`. The response-surface
model is the predictive model and the basis of the design space, and it supersedes the
screening estimates wherever the two differ. Its predictions are mean levels, so a
prediction at the edge of the region carries about a one in two chance of falling on either
side of the predicted value if the variability around the mean is symmetric [@amab2009].
The design space in §6 is therefore not offered as an assurance statement on its own, and
the assurance that a batch meets its criteria comes from the capability analysis in §8.

Lack of fit is not significant for any response. The residual variance was partitioned
against the `{python} rsm_pe_df` pure-error degrees of freedom from the centre points, and
the smallest lack-of-fit p-value across the five responses is
`{python} f"{rsm_lof_p_lo:.2f}"` (`{python} rsm_lof_lo_r.lower()`), well above α = 0.05.
The quadratic form is therefore sufficient to describe the surfaces over the ranges run,
and no evidence was found that a higher-order model is needed. @tbl-anova-gal and
@tbl-anova-hm give the partition for the two responses that drive the design space and the
capability claim.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "galactosylation"))
print()
print(": Analysis of variance with lack-of-fit partition, galactosylation response-surface "
      "model. {#tbl-anova-gal}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "high_mannose"))
print()
print(": Analysis of variance with lack-of-fit partition, high mannose response-surface "
      "model. {#tbl-anova-hm}")
```

The coefficient tables for the same two responses are given in @tbl-coef-gal and
@tbl-coef-hm, and the remaining three are in Appendix C. For galactosylation, the four main
effects, the pH by temperature, pH by duration and pH by pCO₂ interactions are all
significant, and none of the quadratic terms is. The surface is close to a plane with
strong twist, and the twist is what excludes the corner identified in §6. For high mannose
the picture is much simpler, with significant terms for culture pH, culture temperature and
two pH interactions, and no significant curvature.

```{python}

print()
```


@fig-contours shows the fitted surfaces over the two factors that carry the largest

## Mechanistic interpretation

The fitted surfaces follow the mechanisms set out in §2.1 in most respects, and they depart
from them in two. Culture temperature raises galactosylation, where §2.1 expected a lower
temperature to raise it, and culture pH lowers acidic charge variants, where deamidation
chemistry gives the opposite sign. Both are set out below with the coefficients that carry
them. The dominant effect on galactosylation is
culture duration, at `{python} f"{rc('galactosylation','E'):+.2f}"` per coded unit, and it
is negative. Terminal galactosylation is added late in the secretory pathway by
galactosyltransferase, whose activity falls as the culture ages and the intracellular
environment acidifies, so material made in the last days of a long culture carries less
galactose. The negative pCO₂ coefficient of
`{python} f"{rc('galactosylation','C'):+.2f}"` has the same root, since dissolved carbon
dioxide lowers intracellular pH and moves the Golgi away from the optimum for that enzyme.
Culture temperature acts the other way, at
`{python} f"{rc('galactosylation','B'):+.2f}"` per coded unit, so a warmer culture carries
more galactose. That is the reverse of the expectation in §2.1, which took the longer
secretory residence time of a cooler culture to be the dominant route. The fitted sign says
that over the range studied the temperature dependence of the transferase itself outweighs
the residence time, and the screening estimate of
`{python} f"{sc('galactosylation','B'):+.1f}"` percentage points across the range agrees
with the response-surface one.

The pH by duration interaction is the term that forces a multivariate treatment. For both
afucosylation and galactosylation it is large and positive
(`{python} f"{rc('afucosylation','AE'):+.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{rc('galactosylation','AE'):+.2f}"` per coded unit), which means the effect of
raising pH depends on how long the culture is run and can change sign across the duration
range. A univariate range for pH, established at one duration, would not hold at another.
This is the quantitative reason the operating region for this step is stated as a
multivariate region in §6 and not as a set of independent ranges.

High mannose behaves as a simpler system. Its dominant term is culture pH at
`{python} f"{rc('high_mannose','A'):+.2f}"` per coded unit, with culture temperature at
`{python} f"{rc('high_mannose','B'):+.2f}"`. High mannose species are the ones that escape
processing by the mannosidases in the early Golgi, so they accumulate when processing
capacity is limiting relative to secretion flux. Raising pH and lowering temperature both
raise the specific secretion rate relative to that capacity, which is the expected
direction and is what the model shows. Neither pCO₂ nor culture duration has a significant
main effect on this response. Both interact significantly with culture pH, at
`{python} f"{rc('high_mannose','AC'):+.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{rc('high_mannose','AE'):+.2f}"` per coded unit (@tbl-coef-hm), so their
influence is conditional on pH and is small beside the pH main effect. That pattern is
consistent with a limitation set early in the pathway, in the compartment pH acts on rather
than in the later ones.

Acidic charge variants are dominated by pCO₂ at
`{python} f"{rc('acidic_variants','C'):+.2f}"` per coded unit. Deamidation of asparagine
residues is base catalysed, and dissolved carbon dioxide lowers the pH of the culture fluid
in which secreted antibody accumulates, so a higher pCO₂ suppresses the reaction. The pH
main effect does not follow that logic. Culture pH enters the same model at
`{python} f"{rc('acidic_variants','A'):+.2f}"` per coded unit, so a higher controlled pH
gives fewer acidic variants, where base catalysis on its own would give more. The icIEF
acidic peak sums species formed by more than one route, and the fitted sign is a property
of that summed measurement and not of deamidation alone. The attribute is of very low
criticality and the predicted levels stay well inside acceptance across the whole region
(§6), so the departure is recorded here and is not carried further. Aggregate
rises with pH and with duration
(`{python} f"{rc('aggregates_hmw','A'):+.2f}"` and
`{python} f"{rc('aggregates_hmw','E'):+.2f}"` per coded unit), which is consistent with the
release of intracellular material as viability declines and with the reduced colloidal
stability of the molecule at the upper end of the pH range. Neither effect is large enough
to threaten the aggregate limit within the region studied, and cation exchange provides the
polishing step for this attribute in any case (PCR-007).

# Design space

The design space for the production bioreactor is a multivariate region in culture pH,
culture temperature, culture duration and pCO₂, with osmolality at its normal operating
range, over which every attribute the step sets remains within its acceptance criterion. It
is the characterized region of @tbl-params with one corner removed, and that single
exclusion bounds everything else in this section.

One corner of the characterized region fails. With culture pH at
`{python} f"{wc['pH']:g}"`, culture duration at `{python} f"{wc['duration']:g}"` days and
pCO₂ at `{python} f"{wc['co2']:g}"` mmHg, all three at their low edges, and culture
temperature at `{python} f"{wc['temperature']:g}"` °C at its high edge, the fitted model
predicts `{python} ds_bind.lower()` of `{python} f"{wc_val:.2f}"` % against an upper limit
of `{python} f"{bind_hi:g}"` %. The exceedance is `{python} f"{wc_over:.2f}"` percentage
points, and it is an edge of failure in the sense of the case study: a boundary the ranges
were deliberately wide enough to find [@amab2009]. The mechanism is the pH by duration
interaction described in §5.4, reinforced by the low pCO₂ and high temperature edges, each
of which raises galactosylation on its own.

The exclusion is small and it is remote from the operating point. Across a grid of
`{python} _lv` levels in each of the four response-surface factors, which is
`{python} f"{ds_pts:,}"` combinations, the models place all five attributes inside their
acceptance criteria at all but `{python} ds_excl` points. Every one of those points fails on
`{python} ds_bind.lower()`, and no other response fails anywhere in the region. @tbl-nor
evaluates the same models at the `{python} nor_corners` corners of the normal operating
ranges, which is the box the process is actually controlled within.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(nor_tbl)
print()
print(": Predicted attribute levels at the " + str(nor_corners) + " corners of the normal "
      "operating ranges, against the acceptance criterion for each response. {#tbl-nor}")
```

Every attribute stays within its criterion at every corner of the normal operating ranges,
with margin. The criterion column of @tbl-nor states how each limit applies. Acidic charge
variants are judged against their upper limit alone, so the lower figure of the range stated
for them is a range of experience and not an acceptance limit. The highest predicted `{python} ds_bind.lower()` at any corner is
`{python} f"{nor_bind_max:.1f}"` %, leaving `{python} f"{nor_bind_margin:.1f}"` percentage
points to the limit, and the worst-case corner of the design space is
`{python} f"{wc_val - nor_bind_max:.1f}"` percentage points further out again. The three
nested regions are therefore the normal operating ranges inside the design space inside the
knowledge space, which is the nesting described in the case study [@amab2009].

The plane that carries the dominant interaction is drawn in @fig-designspace, with culture
temperature and pCO₂ at their set-points. No part of the excluded corner appears there,
since the exclusion needs culture temperature at its high edge and pCO₂ at its low edge at
the same time. The figure is the plane through the operating point and not the worst-case
plane, and every point in it satisfies all five criteria.

![Production-bioreactor design space in the culture pH by culture duration plane, with culture temperature and pCO₂ at their set-points. The shaded region satisfies all five attribute criteria simultaneously, the contours are afucosylation, the dotted rectangle is the normal operating range and the marker is the set-point. Acceptance boundaries are drawn as dashed lines, and none falls inside this plane.](../outputs/figures/fig_bioreactor_designspace.png){#fig-designspace}

Movement within the design space is not a change from a regulatory filing perspective, as
stated in ICH Q8 [@ichq8]. It remains subject to the pharmaceutical quality system, so a
planned move within the region is assessed prospectively under change control before it is
made [@ichq10]. Movement outside the region, including any operation in the excluded
corner, is a change and requires prior approval.

Three bounds apply to this claim. First, the region is defined only over the ranges
characterized, and no statement is made about conditions outside @tbl-params. Second, the
response-surface model
predicts mean levels of each attribute, so the boundary of the region is a mean-level
boundary and the assurance that a batch meets its criterion comes from the capability
analysis in §8, not from the boundary itself. Third, the region rests on a scale-down model
qualified for this cell line, this medium platform and these ranges, and it has not been
confirmed at commercial scale at its edges. Confirmation at the set-point and within the
normal operating ranges is the object of the process performance qualification.

# Proven acceptable ranges

The proven acceptable ranges complement the design space. Where the design space is the
multivariate region, a proven acceptable range is the range of one parameter over which one
attribute stays within acceptance, and the two answer different questions. The acceptance
criteria used are the drug-substance criteria of @tbl-cqa, which for the five measured
attributes are the study-provided specifications and require no back-calculation. No viral
clearance attribute is in scope at this step, so no step-level floor had to be derived.

@tbl-par gives, for each governed attribute and each response-surface factor, the
characterization range and both analyses described in §3.5.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
print()
print(": Proven acceptable ranges by attribute and parameter. The set-point analysis holds "
      "the other factors at their set-points; the NOR analysis varies them within their "
      "normal operating ranges by Monte-Carlo of the fitted model. {#tbl-par}")
```

Every proven acceptable range in the table spans the full characterization range of its
parameter, under both analyses. No single parameter, moved alone across the whole range
studied, takes any attribute out of specification, and that remains true when the other
three parameters vary randomly within their normal operating ranges. It does not mean that
every combination of parameters is acceptable, and §6 shows one combination that is not.
The binding
constraint on the operating region at this step is the multivariate corner, not any
univariate proven acceptable range.

The reason the two columns agree is that the effects are moderate relative to the width of
the acceptance criteria and the normal operating ranges are narrow. Propagating normal
operating variation in the other three factors widens the predictive interval of each
attribute, but not far enough to reach a limit anywhere along the scanned range. The one
attribute where the two analyses would be expected to separate first is
`{python} ds_bind.lower()`, since it has both the largest effects and the interaction that
produces the excluded corner, and even there the propagated interval stays inside the
criterion.

@fig-par-afu to @fig-par-agg give the analysis for each governed attribute against its
governing parameter, which is the parameter with the largest fitted main effect on that
attribute.
The acceptable region is shaded, the acceptance limits are drawn, and the set-point and
normal operating range are marked. The left panel of each figure is the set-point analysis
and the right panel the Monte-Carlo analysis, with its 95 % predictive interval.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-afu
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for afucosylation against its governing parameter, at the set-point of the other factors (left) and with the other factors varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, "afucosylation", D.governing_factor(UO, "afucosylation"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-gal
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for galactosylation against its governing parameter, at the set-point of the other factors (left) and with the other factors varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, "galactosylation", D.governing_factor(UO, "galactosylation"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hm
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for high mannose against its governing parameter, at the set-point of the other factors (left) and with the other factors varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, "high_mannose", D.governing_factor(UO, "high_mannose"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-acid
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for acidic charge variants against its governing parameter, at the set-point of the other factors (left) and with the other factors varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, "acidic_variants", D.governing_factor(UO, "acidic_variants"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for high molecular weight aggregate against its governing parameter, at the set-point of the other factors (left) and with the other factors varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
D.fig_par(UO, "aggregates_hmw", D.governing_factor(UO, "aggregates_hmw"))
plt.show()
```
