Two bounds apply. The ranges are proven over the characterization ranges of @tbl-params and
against the fitted response-surface model, so they are supported by data only where data
were taken. They are also computed at osmolality within its normal operating range, since
osmolality was not a response-surface factor (§4.3).

# Process capability and robustness

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches, each with every parameter drawn independently
within its normal operating range and each attribute predicted from the fitted models with
their residual variability. @tbl-cap gives the outcome for the seven attributes the step
sets.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(CQA_KEYS))
print()
print(": Predicted commercial-scale capability for the attributes set by the production "
      "bioreactor, from " + f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}" + " simulated batches with all "
      "parameters inside their normal operating ranges. {#tbl-cap}")
```

Every attribute meets its acceptance criterion, and the tightest capability is comfortable.
`{python} tight["cqa"]` is the binding attribute with a one-sided Cpk of
`{python} f"{tight['Cpk']:.2f}"`. Its predicted mean is
`{python} f"{tight['mean']:.2f}"` `{python} tight["unit"]`, which sits
`{python} f"{tight_margin:.2f}"` percentage points above the `{python} tight_side` limit and
`{python} f"{tight_other:.2f}"` percentage points below the other one. That this is the
tightest of the seven follows from the attribute and not from the process, since high
mannose has the narrowest acceptance range of the glycan attributes and the largest relative
variability at the centre point (§5.1). The other two glycan attributes follow at
Cpk values close to `{python} f"{capb.loc[capb.key=='afucosylation','Cpk'].iloc[0]:.1f}"`.

Three of the seven attributes carry capability that is not this step's alone.
`{python} wide["cqa"]` shows the highest index in the table at
`{python} f"{wide['Cpk']:.0f}"`, which reflects the cation exchange polish and not the
culture (PCR-007). The bioreactor delivers aggregate at the level shown at the centre point
in @tbl-cp, and the drug-substance mean is lower than that by a factor of
`{python} f"{agg_ratio:.1f}"`. Host cell
protein and residual DNA are generated in the culture at levels orders of magnitude above
their drug substance criteria, and the indices shown here are the product of clearance at
Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-005, PCR-007, PCR-008). For those three
attributes the contribution of this step is the input level to the purification train, and
that input level is what the culture parameters control.

The capability estimate is bounded in two ways. It assumes every parameter stays inside its
normal operating range, which is what the control system delivers and what the parameter
classifications in §9 commit to. It also rests on the qualified scale-down model, since the
underlying models were fitted to scale-down data. Confirmation at commercial scale is the
object of the process performance qualification and is not claimed here.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified per SOP-4001 from the effects demonstrated in this study and
from the risk of the parameter leaving the design space in routine operation. A parameter
whose variability affects a critical quality attribute is a critical process parameter, and
it is called well controlled when the equipment and the control scheme make an excursion
outside the design space unlikely [@amab2009]. The classifications are given in @tbl-class
and the reasoning follows.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cls_tbl)
print()
print(": Final classification of every production-bioreactor parameter, with the ranges "
      "that support it. {#tbl-class}")
```

- Culture pH is a WC-CPP. It has a significant effect on four of the five measured
  attributes and it is the governing parameter for high mannose and for aggregate. It is
  held by closed-loop control with redundant calibrated probes, and the normal operating
  range is a fraction of the characterized range, so the risk of leaving the design space is
  low.
- Culture temperature is a WC-CPP. It affects galactosylation, high mannose and acidic
  variants, and it interacts with pH. Jacket control holds the culture well within the
  normal operating range and an excursion would be detected within minutes.
- pCO₂ is a WC-CPP. It carries the largest single effect in the screening study, on acidic
  charge variants, and a substantial effect on galactosylation. It is the least tightly
  controlled of the five multivariate parameters, since it depends on sparge efficiency and
  on vessel scale, which is why the characterized range is wide. The classification is well
  controlled and not critical because the proven acceptable range for this parameter spans
  its full characterized range under both analyses (§7), and an excursion beyond that range
  is not physically plausible in the commercial vessel.
- Osmolality is a WC-CPP. It has significant effects on galactosylation and on acidic
  variants in the screening study, and it was not carried into the response-surface design
  (§4.3). It is classified from the screening result and is controlled by the feed and base
  strategy, with at-line monitoring through the culture.
- Culture duration is a WC-CPP. It carries the largest effect on galactosylation and the
  largest main effect on afucosylation, and it is one of the two parameters in the dominant
  interaction. It is set by the harvest
  decision and not by a controller, and the harvest criteria in SOP-2003 bound it
  directly, so the risk of operating outside the range is low.
- Dissolved oxygen is a KPP. It drives peak viable cell density and titre and no effect of
  it on a quality attribute has been demonstrated. It is monitored and controlled because
  process consistency depends on it, which is the purpose a key process parameter serves.
- Initial viable cell concentration is a KPP, on the same basis. It sets the growth
  trajectory and the integral of viable cells, and therefore titre, without a demonstrated
  quality effect.
- Basal medium concentration is a GPP. It affects titre, no effect of it on a quality
  attribute was demonstrated over the range studied (§4.4), and it is controlled by the
  media preparation procedure.
- Nutrient feed-1 volume is a KPP. It is critical to titre and is delivered gravimetrically
  under the control described in §10, following the deviation reported in §13.2.

The step has `{python} n_wccpp` well-controlled critical process parameters,
`{python} n_kpp` key process parameters and `{python} n_gpp` general process parameter. No
parameter of this step is classified as a critical process parameter. That outcome rests on
control capability rather than on the absence of effects, since four of the five
multivariate parameters have large demonstrated effects. The commercial vessel holds each
of them within a normal operating range that sits well inside the design space, and the
capability analysis in §8 quantifies what that containment delivers.

# Contribution to the control strategy

This step contributes the elements of the control strategy that govern the formation of the
glycan, charge variant and aggregate attributes. They are as follows.

- The five multivariate parameters are controlled to the normal operating ranges in
  @tbl-params, and the design space of §6 defines the region within which they may be moved
  under the quality system.
- Culture pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and pCO₂ are monitored continuously by
  calibrated in-process instrumentation, and osmolality is monitored at line. Viable cell
  density, viability and titre are trended daily against the platform profile given in
  §3.2.
- Harvest is bounded by the criteria in SOP-2003, which controls culture duration directly
  and is the control that keeps the aggregate and host cell protein input to the
  purification train within the characterized range.
- Nutrient feed-1 is delivered gravimetrically with mass reconciliation after each addition,
  and the feed pump is verified before each campaign. This control was strengthened after
  DEV-003-02 (§13.2).
- Released N-glycan mapping, size variants, charge variants, host cell protein and residual
  DNA are tested on the drug substance under the methods of @tbl-methods. Testing confirms
  the outcome; it does not control it, and the control rests on the parameter ranges above.
- The scale-down model is maintained under SOP-1001 so that any future range change can be
  assessed on a qualified system and not at scale.

The step does not deliver the drug substance specification for aggregate, host cell protein
or residual DNA on its own. What it delivers for those three attributes is a bounded input
to the purification train, and the clearance that turns that input into the drug substance
levels of @tbl-cap is characterized in PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. The overall control
strategy, including how the elements of this step combine with the downstream ones, is
consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is well understood over the ranges characterized, and the understanding is
mechanistic and not merely empirical. Most of the significant main effects in @tbl-screff
run through a route in the secretory pathway or in culture chemistry that was set out
before the study was run (§2.1), and the fitted models reproduce those routes in direction.
Two main effects do not. Culture temperature raises galactosylation where a lower
temperature was expected to raise it, and culture pH lowers acidic charge variants where
deamidation chemistry gives the opposite sign, and §5.4 sets both out. The study also
returned significant interactions that §2.1 did not anticipate, since prior knowledge
carried the pH by duration term alone. What the study added there was the size of that
term, which is what makes a multivariate operating region necessary rather than convenient.

The adverse finding of the study is the excluded corner. At the low edges of pH, duration
and pCO₂ with temperature high, galactosylation is predicted at
`{python} f"{wc_val:.2f}"` % against a limit of `{python} f"{bind_hi:g}"` %. That corner is
excluded from the design space, and no operation there is permitted without prior approval.
Two things bound its practical significance. It requires four parameters to sit
simultaneously at the edges of ranges that are between `{python} f"{wid_rsm_lo:.1f}"` and
`{python} f"{wid_rsm_hi:.1f}"` times the width of their normal operating ranges, and the normal
operating ranges themselves leave `{python} f"{nor_bind_margin:.1f}"` percentage
points of margin at their worst corner (@tbl-nor). The finding does not weaken the design
space claim. It is the reason the claim can be stated as a region rather than as an
assumption.

Confidence in the scale-down model is good but not unlimited. The model is geometrically
similar to the commercial vessel and matches it on the scale-independent parameters, and
the scale-dependent parameters were set on performance and not on setting (§3.1). Its
qualification covers this cell line, this medium platform and these ranges. Two known
differences remain. Carbon dioxide accumulates less readily at small scale than in a
commercial vessel, which is the reason the pCO₂ range was carried to
`{python} f"{pset('co2','hi'):g}"` mmHg instead of stopping at the range seen at
laboratory scale. Mixing time also scales with vessel size, so gradients that are absent at
small scale can exist at commercial scale. Both are managed by the process performance
qualification, which measures the same attributes on commercial batches.

Three further limitations should be read with the conclusions. The response-surface model
predicts mean levels and its edges carry no assurance statement on their own, which is why
the capability analysis exists (§5.3, §8). Osmolality was characterized in screening only,
so its contribution to the region is bounded by a two-level estimate and is not described
by a surface (§4.3). The univariate parameters were assessed against process performance,
so the quality claims of this report rest on the multivariate work alone (§4.4). None of
the three affects the classification of any parameter.

Two deviations occurred during execution and both were retained. A pCO₂ probe drifted
between calibrations on one screening run, and one centre-point batch received less
nutrient feed than the schedule specifies. The magnitudes are small against the ranges
studied, the impact assessments are in §13, and neither changed an effect estimate, a
classification or the boundary of the operating region. No parameter of this step required
the most stringent level of control, and the argument for that is control capability rather
than an absence of effects (§9).

# Conclusions

The production bioreactor is characterized and the step is robust over the ranges studied.
A response-surface model over culture pH, culture temperature, culture duration and pCO₂
defines a multivariate design space in which the five measured attributes remain within
their acceptance criteria, with one corner of the characterized region excluded on
`{python} ds_bind.lower()`. The normal operating ranges lie well inside that region, with
`{python} f"{nor_bind_margin:.1f}"` percentage points of margin on the binding attribute at
the worst corner of the operating box.

Proven acceptable ranges span the full characterization range of every response-surface
parameter against every attribute it governs, under both the set-point and the
normal-operating-range analyses, so the
constraint that binds the operating region is the multivariate corner and not a univariate
range. Predicted commercial-scale capability meets acceptance for all seven attributes the
step sets, with `{python} tight["cqa"]` the tightest at a one-sided Cpk of
`{python} f"{tight['Cpk']:.2f}"` and `{python} f"{tight_margin:.2f}"` percentage points to
its binding limit. The study classified `{python} n_param` parameters, `{python} n_wccpp` of
them as well-controlled critical process parameters and none as a critical process
parameter.
Two deviations were investigated and resolved without impact on any of these outcomes.

Two claims are not made here. The design space has not been confirmed at commercial scale
at its edges, and confirmation within the normal operating ranges is the object of the
process performance qualification. The drug substance levels of aggregate, host cell
protein and residual DNA depend on downstream clearance as well as on culture conditions,
and the credit for that clearance belongs to PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008. The outcomes of
this report are consolidated with those of the other steps in PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan

Two deviations from PCP-003 were recorded during execution. Each was raised at the time of
detection, investigated to root cause, assessed for impact on the study conclusions and
closed. Both were dispositioned as retained, meaning the affected run stayed in the
analysis. @tbl-dev is the register.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Deviations recorded during execution of the production-bioreactor "
      "characterization. {#tbl-dev}")
```

The two entries are of different kinds. The first is an instrument drift affecting one
factor setting on one screening run, and the second is a materials delivery shortfall on a
centre-point batch. Neither affected a response-surface run. The subsections below give the
adverse finding, the investigation and the impact assessment for each.

## DEV-003-01 — dissolved carbon dioxide probe drift

The in-process pCO₂ probe read `{python} f"{dev_003_01_offset_mmhg:g}"` mmHg below the
offline reference on screening run 4, so that run was executed at a true pCO₂ above its
assigned setting. The discrepancy was found by the routine comparison of the in-process
reading against an offline blood gas measurement, and it was confirmed on the retained
sample.

The investigation attributed the discrepancy to drift of the probe between scheduled
calibrations. The probe is part of instrumented system EQ-BRX-205, whose calibration status
at the time of execution is given in @tbl-equip. The probe was within its calibration
interval when the run was executed, which is why the drift was not detected by the
calibration programme, and it was recalibrated against the offline reference before the
response-surface design was executed.
No other run in either design showed a comparable discrepancy.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_eq = equipment_df()
show(_eq[_eq["Equipment"] == "EQ-BRX-205"])
print()
print(": Calibration record of the instrumented scale-down system affected by DEV-003-01. "
      "{#tbl-equip}")
```

The impact assessment bounds the consequence on the fitted effects. The offset corresponds
to `{python} f"{dev1_coded:.2f}"` coded units on the pCO₂ axis, which is a small fraction
of the distance from the set-point to the edge of the characterization range. Evaluating
the fitted response-surface model at the set-point with pCO₂ displaced by that amount moves
the most pCO₂-sensitive response, `{python} LAB[dev1_worst_r].lower()`, by
`{python} f"{dev1_worst:.2f}"` percentage points. That shift is smaller than the
centre-point standard deviation of the same response,
`{python} f"{dev1_sd:.2f}"` percentage points (@tbl-cp), so it is not resolvable against
the reproducibility of the study. The run was retained. The true setting remained inside
the characterization range of pCO₂, the direction of every screening effect is unchanged,
and the design space of §6 rests on the response-surface design, which the deviation does
not touch.

## DEV-003-02 — nutrient feed-1 under-delivery

One centre-point batch of the screening design received
`{python} f"{dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct:g}"` % less nutrient feed-1 than the schedule
specifies, which is a delivered volume of `{python} f"{dev2_delivered:.1f}"` % of working
volume against a set-point of `{python} f"{feed_sp:g}"` %. The shortfall was found after
execution by mass reconciliation of feed lot LOT-FED-3120 against the batch record, not by
an in-process alarm.

Root cause was a calibration offset on the feed pump, which delivered consistently below
its commanded volume across the campaign period. The pump was recalibrated and the delivery
verification described in §10 was introduced as a preventive action. The shortfall is a
materials deviation and not a parameter excursion in the design, since nutrient feed-1
volume is a univariate parameter and was held at its set-point in every designed run.

The impact assessment compared the affected batch against `{python} dev_003_02_ver_n`
verification runs executed at the centre point after the pump was recalibrated, with the
released glycan attributes measured by AMV-3010. The half width of the 95 % confidence
interval on the difference is `{python} f"{dev_003_02_ci_hw:g}"` % relative, and the
observed difference lies inside it, so no difference in the glycan profile was
demonstrated. The delivered volume of `{python} f"{dev2_delivered:.1f}"` % of working
volume also remains inside the normal operating range of that parameter, which is
`{python} f"{pset('feed_vol','nor_lo'):g}"` to
`{python} f"{pset('feed_vol','nor_hi'):g}"` % (@tbl-params).

The batch was retained as a centre point. Retaining it slightly inflates the pure-error term
of the screening design, which is conservative, since a larger pure error makes a
lack-of-fit test easier to pass and the screening design is not used for prediction in any
case (§5.2). The lack-of-fit tests that support the design space come from the
response-surface design, whose `{python} cp_rsm` centre points were unaffected. No effect
estimate, no classification and no boundary of the operating region was changed by this
deviation.

# Appendix A — Screening design matrix and responses {.unnumbered}

The coded settings of the `{python} n_scr` screening runs are given in @tbl-appa1 and the
measured responses in @tbl-appa2. Factor codes are given in @tbl-legend, and the coded
levels minus one, zero and plus one correspond to the low edge, the set-point and the high
edge of each characterization range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_a = D.coded_matrix_df(UO, "screening")
_labels = [LAB[r] for r in RESP]
show(_a[[c for c in _a.columns if c not in _labels]])
print()
print(": Screening design, coded factor settings by run. {#tbl-appa1}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(_a[["Run", "Type"] + _labels])
print()
print(": Screening design, measured responses by run. {#tbl-appa2}")
```

# Appendix B — Response-surface design matrix and responses {.unnumbered}

The coded settings of the `{python} n_rsm` response-surface runs are given in @tbl-appb1
and the measured responses in @tbl-appb2. Runs of type factorial are the cube points, axial
runs sit on the faces of the cube, and centre runs are at the set-point of every factor.

```{python}

show(_b[[c for c in _b.columns if c not in _labels]])
print()
print(": Response-surface design, coded factor settings by run. {#tbl-appb1}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(_b[["Run", "Type"] + _labels])
print()
print(": Response-surface design, measured responses by run. {#tbl-appb2}")
```

The complete screening effect tables for all `{python} n_resp` responses are given first,
followed by the response-surface coefficient tables for the three responses not shown in

model order in the coefficient tables.
